abbreviations.description: Resembles "seek you" when pronounced. Used when calling any station.

examples.explanation: *call* calls any station and invites anyone to answer.

phrases.meaning: Your RST (Readability, Signal, Tone) report is ...
phrases.description: A standard message containing an RST report for the receiving station.

examples.explanation: *call* gives K1ABC a RST report of 599. Perfectly clear & strong signal, perfect tone.

phrases.description: Usually heard at the end of a QSO. 'FER' is used instead of 'FOR' to save time.

examples.message: W2XYZ DE *call* UR RST 599 599 TNX FER QSO
examples.explanation: *call* thanks W2XYZ for the contact after giving them an RST report.

prosigns.description: Invites the adressed station to respond.

qcodes.description:
QTH ... - My location is ...
QTH? - What is your location?
Used to refer to an contact between two stations. Usually involves an exchange of RS(T) reports. Used in Morse and Phone transmissions.
